findings.title: Mobile registration accepts a caller-provided web address
findings.plain: A mobile setup helper may contact an address supplied by the caller, exposing a private service or credentials.
findings.verify_by: Run it with an untrusted address and confirm it is rejected or limited to Apple hosts.
findings.evidence: Both helpers build requests from a caller-provided path or address; allowed host and redirect rules need confirmation.
findings.correction: Allow only fixed Apple hosts and reject absolute addresses before requests.
findings.test_plan: Test allowed Apple paths and rejected private or external addresses.

findings.title: Generated command documentation may use stale state
findings.plain: The command reference may describe earlier settings, so Atlas can appear to support a command that no longer works.
findings.verify_by: Change one command entry, regenerate, and confirm the new wording appears.
findings.evidence: The generator carries pending entries while reading the catalog; a flagged state pattern needs a focused regeneration check.
findings.correction: Reload the working entry at each boundary and add a regeneration check.
findings.test_plan: Regenerate after a temporary catalog change and compare output.

findings.title: Secret-like values are present in tracked material
findings.plain: A secret-like value appears in tracked Atlas material; if real, it could expose private data.
findings.verify_by: Inspect flagged values without exposing them and confirm they are synthetic or rotate any real credential.
findings.owner_action: Confirm whether any flagged value is real and rotate it outside Atlas if so.
findings.stopgap: Do not use any flagged credential; revoke it if real.
findings.evidence: Secret-shaped values were found in a work-log test and two fixtures; confirm they are synthetic.
findings.correction: Remove real credentials, replace fixtures with placeholders, and add a scan gate.
findings.test_plan: Run the secret scan after replacement and confirm no usable credential remains.
findings.control: Secrets must not be committed or retained in logs.

findings.title: Input paths still contain panic-prone unwraps
findings.plain: Some input or state paths may panic instead of returning a controlled failure.
findings.verify_by: Exercise flagged paths with missing and malformed values and confirm an error is returned.
findings.evidence: The scanner found unwrap calls in input-handling code; each call needs a focused check.
findings.correction: Replace unsafe unwraps with explicit error propagation where input is untrusted.
findings.test_plan: Run targeted failure cases and the existing Rust test suite.

findings.title: Numeric conversions may silently lose values
findings.plain: Some numeric conversions may truncate or overflow without a user-visible error.
findings.verify_by: Exercise boundary values and confirm invalid conversions fail clearly.
findings.evidence: The scanner found lossy casts in shipped Rust code; boundary behavior needs confirmation.
findings.correction: Use checked conversions or explicit range handling.
findings.test_plan: Run boundary-value tests for each affected path.

findings.title: Some operation failures may be ignored
findings.plain: Ignored results can make Atlas report progress when an operation actually failed.
findings.verify_by: Force the flagged operation to fail and confirm the failure reaches status and logs.
findings.evidence: The scanner found ignored results in shipped Rust code.
findings.correction: Handle or explicitly document every result according to the operation contract.
findings.test_plan: Run forced-failure checks for affected operations.

findings.title: State imports may accept unknown fields silently
findings.plain: Persisted state may load while ignoring fields it does not understand, hiding corruption or version drift.
findings.verify_by: Load state containing an unknown field and confirm the chosen compatibility behavior is explicit.
findings.evidence: The scanner found many deserializers without an explicit unknown-field policy.
findings.correction: Choose and test strict rejection or deliberate migration handling.
findings.test_plan: Run state compatibility tests with unknown and missing fields.

findings.title: Missing state can fall back to defaults without clear status
findings.plain: A missing or unreadable state file may be treated as a fresh default, risking silent loss of continuity.
findings.verify_by: Remove or corrupt state and confirm Atlas reports the condition and preserves recoverability.
findings.evidence: The scanner found defaulting state reads in shipped Rust code.
findings.correction: Surface the read failure and require an explicit recovery path.
findings.test_plan: Run missing, corrupt, and permission-denied state checks.
